issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Rideable.messageOnRide() to be a no-argument method that returns a String (and the template's Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no argument), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it in Pig and Seal with a String parameter. This parameter mismatch creates a structural inconsistency: students following the problem/template will implement/use a no-arg method, while the solution uses a different signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the String parameter: define Rideable.messageOnRide() and implement Pig/Seal.messageOnRide() with no parameters returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement, template Main, and all descriptions to require a parameter (e.g., equipment) and demonstrate calling messageOnRide with that argument. Prefer fix (A) to preserve the current exercise description and template behavior.

issues.description: The Rideable interface's messageOnRide method is defined without parameters in the problem statement and the template usage (calls to r.messageOnRide()), but the solution repository declares messageOnRide(String equipment). This signature mismatch (no-arg vs. one-arg) creates a conceptual and practical mapping problem: students are instructed to implement/consume a no-argument messageOnRide(), yet the solution uses a different identifier/signature that requires an equipment parameter and changes the expected return format. This inconsistency can cause compilation errors for code that follows the template/problem and adds unnecessary cognitive burden to map the two variants.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) change the solution to declare messageOnRide() with no parameters and update implementations (Pig, Seal) to return 'Riding on [Animal Type] [name]' (no equipment), matching the UML and template usage; or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust the UML and textual description accordingly. Option (A) is recommended to align with the current problem specification and template calls.
